newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-FIFTH SEED HUBER SURVIVES AUSTRALIAN OPEN SCARE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-FIFTH SEED HUBER SURVIVES AUSTRALIAN OPEN SCARE.

text.p: German women's fifth seed Anke Huber almost followed compatriot Boris Becker out of the Australian Open on Tuesday, surviving a tight three-setter against American Amy Frazier.
Huber, losing finalist to Monica Seles in last year's Open, lost the first set 6-0 but fought back to win 0-6 6-2 7-5, overcoming a last set comeback from the unseeded Frazier.

Having levelled the match at one set each, Huber took a 4-1 lead in the decider when Frazier, a quarter-finalist in Melbourne in 1992, again came back to break the German's serve and level the set at 4-4.
Urged on by a capacity crowd, Huber kept her nerve in the blustery, hot conditions on an outside court to stave off the American, who also made the fourth round of Wimbledon last year.
Huber will next meet the winner of the first-round tie between Francesca Lubiani of Italy and Rachel McQuillan of Australia.
Becker, the defending men's champion, lost out to Spanish clay court specialist Carlos Moya on Monday.
